newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Stocks and Stocks sees progress this year.
newsitem.headline: Stocks and Stocks sees progress this year.

text.p: South Africa's Stocks and Stocks Ltd, fresh from posting a drop in year profit, said on Thursday that it would make progress in its current financial year as growth of the country's economy starts to pick up.

"We view this next year in a positive light. Our order book and plans, plus the positive signs in the economy, make us confident that our next year's results will be back on track," the company said in statement.
Earlier the firm, a hotel builder, posted a drop in earnings per share to 49 cents for the year ended April 30 from 69 cents and cut its dividend by a third from 15 cents to ten cents.
Stocks said sustained high interest rates had taken a heavy toll on its business, hitting profits and hampering growth.

However, the firm said it was fairly certain interest rates would come down in the second half of (calendar) 1997 and continue to fall during 1998. "The business mood for next year is positive," the firm said.
Chairman Reg Edwards said the current year would see group debt levels come down and it would also benefit from a new policy of more autonomous management at its five operating divisions.
